content.text:
Silhouette: Horizontal red fox frame carried on two hind legs, barn owl wings in place of the forelegs. Host frame: the red fox sets the outline, body size and overall frame. It is a single creature combining a red fox and a barn owl. The head is that of the red fox, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: red fox body and legs with its own dense fur on the face, back, flanks, belly, hips, legs and tail; plain coat with no stripes or spots. From the barn owl, as parts and materials on the red fox's own body: broad wings of layered flight feathers in place of the forelegs, standing on two hind legs, wings sized for flight; layered contour feathers in its own colors grown from the skin as the red fox's own covering over the shoulders and neck, replacing the red fox's dense fur there and conforming to the red fox's body, sized to the red fox's body and following its contours. Every covered part keeps the red fox's own length and shape; the dense fur stops at the covering's edge, and the face, back, flanks, belly, hips, legs and tail keep the red fox's own dense fur; deep keel and heavy flight chest. The covering follows the body's own shape. Bilaterally symmetrical, with recognizable limbs and visible sense organs. Habitat cue (desert): larger ears and longer tail for shedding heat. Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

summary.text:
**Designing fox-owl hybrid**
I'm planning the silhouette by combining a red fox body and head with barn owl wings in place of forelegs, keeping the fox outline, dense fur, and clear eyes while sizing the layered wings for a two-legged stance.
**Refining hybrid illustration details**
I'm organizing the natural history illustration with a red fox body, barn owl wings and shoulder feathers, desert cues, and a plain light background in a side three-quarter view.
**Regenerating two-legged hybrid**
I'm fixing the illustration so the creature shows only two hind legs and no forelegs, then regenerating to match that requirement.
